s.n: Parade chestnuts in sage brown butter
s.note: warming up along the 1947 Thanksgiving parade route
s.how: Cut a cross in the flat side of 600g chestnuts and soak in water for 10 minutes. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes until the shells open, then wrap in a tea towel for 5 minutes and peel while warm. Melt 60g butter until it foams and turns nutty brown, add 12 sage leaves and fry until crisp. Toss in the chestnuts with 1 tbsp maple syrup and flaky salt.

s.note: the sacks of letters dumped on the judge's bench
s.how: Beat 250g cream cheese with 50g blue cheese and snipped chives until smooth. Cut celery into short sticks and pipe or spoon the filling along each. Serve on a platter beside crackers topped with slices of vintage cheddar, the way a 1940s party did it.

m.n: Fred Gailey's New York pot roast
m.note: the lawyer across the hall who takes Kris's case
m.how: Sear a 1.5kg piece of beef chuck all over. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots and 2 celery sticks, then 250ml red wine and enough water to come halfway. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g potatoes for the last hour. Slice and serve with the juices.

w.note: Christmas in the house Susan wished for
w.how: Soak 500g mixed dried fruit in 100ml brandy overnight. Mix with 125g melted butter, 125g brown sugar, 2 eggs, breadcrumbs, flour and mixed spice. Steam in a greased basin for 4 hours. Warm a little brandy, pour over, light at the table and serve with custard.

d.how: Pour 1.5 litres cloudy apple juice into a pot with 3 tbsp maple syrup, 2 cinnamon sticks, 3 star anise, 6 cloves and 1 sliced orange. Bring to a simmer, then keep just below simmering for 20 minutes. Strain into mugs and add a cinnamon stick and an orange slice studded with cloves to each.
